title: Normal equations from your three points
summary: A recap built from your own example. Skim it if it feels familiar.

blocks.title: A guess, scored

define.meaning: $r = b - Ax$: data minus fit, one entry per point.

blocks.why: The best line is the one that makes $\|r\|^2$ smallest. You scored guesses this way before; this warms the numbers up.
blocks.prompt: Your points are $(1, 1)$, $(2, 2)$, $(3, 6)$, fitted by $y = c + mx$. For the guess $y = x$ ($c = 0$, $m = 1$), what is $\|r\|^2$?
hints: The line $y = x$ predicts 1, 2 and 3 at the three points.
Data minus fit: $r = (1 - 1,\; 2 - 2,\; 6 - 3)$. Square each entry and add.

check.say: Set the line in the picture to $c = 0$, $m = 1$ and read $\|r\|^2$ under it.

blocks.solution: 9, as before. Your other guesses scored 6.5 ($y = 1 + 1.5x$) and 6 ($y = 1 + x$).

blocks.title: AᵀA

define.meaning: Each entry is a dot product of two columns of $A$: row $i$, column $j$ is (column $i$) · (column $j$).

blocks.why: At the best fit the residual is perpendicular to every column of $A$. Written out, that is $A^\mathsf{T}A\,x = A^\mathsf{T}b$: the normal equations.
blocks.prompt: $A = \begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&2\\1&3\end{bmatrix}$, one column per unknown ($c$, then $m$). Write $A^\mathsf{T}A$.
hints: Row 1, column 2 is $(1,1,1)\cdot(1,2,3)$. Row 2, column 2 is $(1,2,3)\cdot(1,2,3)$.

check.say: $A^\mathsf{T}A$ always equals its own transpose, so the top-right and bottom-left must match. The top-left is the number of points.

blocks.solution: Symmetric, as it must be: the same matrix you built before.

blocks.title: Aᵀb
blocks.why: The right-hand side of the normal equations: how much of $b$ lies along each column.
blocks.prompt: Each entry of $A^\mathsf{T}b$ is a column of $A$ dotted with $b = (1, 2, 6)$. Write $A^\mathsf{T}b$.

check.say: Addition slips are the easiest ones to make here. Add the products one at a time in the calculator.

blocks.title: Solve them
blocks.why: Two equations, two unknowns, and $A^\mathsf{T}A$ is invertible here: exactly one best line.

slips.say: Look at $6(3 - 2m)$: the 6 multiplies both terms, the $3$ and the $-2m$.

hints: Divide the first equation by 3 to get $c$ on its own.
$c = 3 - 2m$. Put that into the second equation.

check.say: Put your $c$ and $m$ back into both equations; both sides should match each time.

blocks.solution: A negative intercept, which no guess near the data would have found.

blocks.title: The residual
blocks.why: The whole derivation rests on $r$ being perpendicular to the columns. Here you can see it.

answer.acceptNote: That is fit − data, the other sign convention. It's fine: it is $-r$, and everything after works the same.

hints: The prediction at $x = 1$ is $-2 + 2.5$; at $x = 2$ it is $-2 + 5$.

check.say: Dot $r$ with each column of $A$. At the best fit both come to 0: that is the condition you started from.

blocks.title: How good is the best?
blocks.why: Comparing with your guesses shows how much the derivation bought.
blocks.prompt: What is $\|r\|^2$ for the best line? Your best guess scored 6.
hints: Square each entry of $r$ and add.
Two entries are $\pm\tfrac12$ and one is $\pm1$.

check.say: Keep a few guesses in the table, then show the best line. Its $r\cdot(1,1,1)$ and $r\cdot x$ are both 0.

blocks.solution: 1.5 against 6: the best line is the one whose residual is perpendicular to both columns.

sideQuest.title: Check it in numpy
sideQuest.body:
Only if you want to; nothing in the course needs it.

```
import numpy as np
A = np.array([[1, 1], [1, 2], [1, 3]])
b = np.array([1, 2, 6])
x, rr, rank, s = np.linalg.lstsq(A, b, rcond=None)
print(x, rr)  # [-2.  2.5] [1.5]
```
